lines.text: Every time you tap a credit card, at least three companies get paid. Even if you pay your bill in full.

lines.text: Credit cards are one of the most profitable businesses in America. Today: exactly where the money comes from, and who really pays for it.
lines.say: Credit cards are one of the most profitable businesses in America. Today: exactly where the money comes from, and who really pays for it.

lines.text: Chapter 1. The swipe.
lines.say: Chapter one. The swipe.

lines.text: Say you buy a $100 pair of shoes. The store doesn't get $100.
lines.say: Say you buy a hundred dollar pair of shoes. The store doesn't get a hundred dollars.

lines.text: The store pays a processing fee, usually a few percent. For a credit card, often around $2 to $3 on $100.
lines.say: The store pays a processing fee, usually a few percent. For a credit card, often around two to three dollars on a hundred.

lines.text: The biggest piece is the interchange fee. It goes to the bank that gave you the card.
lines.say: The biggest piece is the interchange fee. It goes to the bank that gave you the card.

lines.text: Across the U.S., merchants paid $198 billion in card processing fees in 2025, a record.
lines.say: Across the U.S., merchants paid a hundred and ninety-eight billion dollars in card processing fees in twenty twenty-five, a record.

lines.text: That's money made on every swipe, no matter whether you ever pay a cent of interest.
lines.say: That's money made on every swipe, no matter whether you ever pay a cent of interest.

lines.text: Chapter 2. The network.
lines.say: Chapter two. The network.

lines.text: Now the network: Visa and Mastercard. Here's the surprising part. Visa doesn't lend you anything.
lines.say: Now the network: Visa and Mastercard. Here's the surprising part. Visa doesn't lend you anything.

lines.text: Your bank lends the money. Visa runs the pipes that move the payment, and charges a small fee on each one.
lines.say: Your bank lends the money. Visa runs the pipes that move the payment, and charges a small fee on each one.

lines.text: Tiny fees on billions of payments add up. In fiscal 2025, Visa's net revenue was $40 billion.
lines.say: Tiny fees on billions of payments add up. In fiscal twenty twenty-five, Visa's net revenue was forty billion dollars.

lines.text: And its net income was $20.1 billion. About half of every dollar it took in was profit.
lines.say: And its net income was twenty point one billion dollars. About half of every dollar it took in was profit.

lines.text: Very few big companies keep that much. That's the power of owning the road every payment has to drive on.

lines.text: Chapter 3. The interest.
lines.say: Chapter three. The interest.

lines.text: Now the biggest money maker for card banks: interest on balances people don't pay off.
lines.say: Now the biggest money maker for card banks: interest on balances people don't pay off.

lines.text: Americans owe $1.26 trillion on credit cards, according to the New York Fed.
lines.say: Americans owe one point two six trillion dollars on credit cards, according to the New York Fed.

lines.text: And on accounts that pay interest, the average rate was 22.15%.
lines.say: And on accounts that pay interest, the average rate was twenty-two point one five percent.

lines.text: Carry a $5,000 balance at that rate for a year, and that's about $1,100 in interest. Roughly $92 a month.
lines.say: Carry a five thousand dollar balance at that rate for a year, and that's about eleven hundred dollars in interest. Roughly ninety-two dollars a month.

lines.text: Then there are fees: annual fees, late fees, cash advance fees, balance transfer fees.
lines.say: Then there are fees: annual fees, late fees, cash advance fees, balance transfer fees.

lines.text: Chapter 4. Who pays for rewards.
lines.say: Chapter four. Who pays for rewards.

lines.text: So who pays for your points and cash back? Mostly, those swipe fees.
lines.say: So who pays for your points and cash back? Mostly, those swipe fees.

lines.text: Stores build card fees into their prices, so everyone pays a little, even people paying cash.
lines.say: Stores build card fees into their prices, so everyone pays a little, even people paying cash.

lines.text: And people who carry a balance pay interest that helps fund the whole system.
lines.say: And people who carry a balance pay interest that helps fund the whole system.

lines.text: Earning 2% back means little if you're paying 22% on a balance.
lines.say: Earning two percent back means little if you're paying twenty-two percent on a balance.

lines.text: On most cards, paying the full statement balance on time means no interest on purchases.
lines.say: On most cards, paying the full statement balance on time means no interest on purchases.

lines.text: Chapter 5. How to pay them nothing.
lines.say: Chapter five. How to pay them nothing.

lines.text: Now the good news. You can use a credit card and pay the card company zero dollars in interest and fees.
lines.say: Now the good news. You can use a credit card and pay the card company zero dollars in interest and fees.

lines.text: Most cards give you a grace period: pay the full statement balance by the due date, and purchases cost no interest.
lines.say: Most cards give you a grace period: pay the full statement balance by the due date, and purchases cost no interest.

lines.text: By law, if a card has a grace period, your bill has to arrive at least 21 days before the payment is due.
lines.say: By law, if a card has a grace period, your bill has to arrive at least twenty-one days before the payment is due.

lines.text: So how do credit card companies make money from everyone?

post.title: How Credit Card Companies Make Money From Everyone
post.yt_desc:
Every card swipe pays at least three companies, even if you pay your bill in full. We follow the money: the $198 billion in processing fees U.S. merchants paid in 2025, how Visa turned $40 billion of revenue into $20.1 billion of profit without lending a dime, the 22.15% average interest rate on $1.26 trillion of card balances, the fees, who really pays for your rewards, and how to use a card while paying the card company nothing.
